name: Meru Health
one_liner: A 12-week app-based program for depression, anxiety and burnout with a dedicated licensed therapist, in-app chat and video sessions.
best_for: Adults with mild to moderate depression, anxiety or burnout who want a structured 12-week program
People whose health plan or employer covers Meru Health
People who like daily app lessons plus messaging with a therapist between video sessions
Teens 13+ whose parent or guardian enrolls them
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988 (Meru Health is not a crisis service)
People who want open-ended weekly video therapy rather than a time-limited program
short_description: A 12-week smartphone program for depression, anxiety and burnout, guided by a licensed therapist, often covered by health plans or employers.
long_description: Meru Health runs a 12-week, app-based treatment program for depression, anxiety and burnout. You start with a video intake with a licensed therapist who stays with you through the program. Each week has short pre-recorded lessons and practices drawing on mindfulness-based therapy, cognitive behavioral therapy and behavioral activation, plus sleep and nutrition guidance. You can message your therapist in the app and schedule a limited number of video sessions (Meru's FAQ says up to four during the program). Participants get a heart-rate-variability biofeedback device for breathing practice and can join an anonymous peer community. Meru Health is offered through some health plans and employers; it also accepts self-pay and HSA/FSA, but does not publish a self-pay price. Teens 13+ can be enrolled by a parent or guardian. In May 2026 the company announced Meru Health Advanced, a program for adults with more complex or treatment-resistant conditions.
patient_summary: You get a 12-week program on your phone: weekly lessons and practices, a biofeedback breathing device, and a licensed therapist you can message and meet by video. You start by checking your insurance or employer coverage on Meru's sign-up page, or choosing to pay yourself, then booking an intake call. It is not a crisis service.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance or free through some employers; self-pay price not published
pricing.notes: Covered by some health plans (e.g. Harvard Pilgrim, Moda) and offered free as a benefit by some employers and plans; cost otherwise depends on your copay and deductible. Meru says it accepts self-pay and HSA/FSA but does not list a self-pay price.

privacy.notes: Clinical records are PHI under HIPAA via Meru's medical groups, but the policy lets third-party cookies on its websites and apps be used for interest-based advertising.
